## Step 0128 — AArch64 sign-extending load derived-opcode contract

- Scope: after Step 0127 the AArch64 dispatcher `ARM64_SIM_L_EXEC` routed every
  arm through a generated membership macro and both operand-source selections
  through a generated selector, but one decision remained inline: the LDRSB,
  LDRSW and LDRSH arms each derived the sign-extending opcode handed to the
  shared extract/reverse/extend contract with a raw opcode ternary. Shared JSON
  spec `kprog/formal/arm64_ldrsx_op_spec.json` (`schema_version` 1, operation
  `arm64LdrsxOp`, three loads in dispatcher order `ldrSb`/`ldrSw`/`ldrSh`, each
  with its `ARM64_OP_LDRS*` opcode, the `sxtb`/`sxtw`/`sxth` sign opcode it
  selects and the sign bit position it signs from) drives generator
  `kprog/formal/generate_arm64_ldrsx_op_spec.py`, which renders six code-drift
  rows and the derived-opcode selector into `generated/arm64_ldrsx_op.h` and the
  `LdrSxLoad` inductive, load-code/sign-code/sign-bits tables into
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64LdrsxOp.lean`.
- The generated macro `KPROG_ARM64_LDRSX_SXOP(OP, UNSUPPORTED)` is a statement
  expression (usable in the arm body but not at file scope or inside
  `_Static_assert`): it seeds its result with `0`, then `switch (OP)` selects
  `ARM64_OP_SXTB` on `case 54U`, `ARM64_OP_SXTW` on `case 57U` and
  `ARM64_OP_SXTH` on `case 63U`, forwarding every other opcode to the
  caller-supplied `UNSUPPORTED` arm. OP is evaluated exactly once. Unlike the
  two-member pairs of Steps 0125/0127 this is a three-way load→sign-extend map.
  The header also emits one `_Static_assert(ARM64_OP_X == N)` code-drift row per
  load and per sign opcode. The generator's `--check` re-reads
  `kprog/arm64/arm64_sim.h` for all six `ARM64_OP_*` numbers, asserts the spec
  table matches and the load/sign-bits orders are `["ldrSb","ldrSw","ldrSh"]`
  and `[8, 32, 16]`, and asserts the live `ARM64_SIM_L_EXEC` region routes the
  derived opcode through `ARM64_SIM_L_LDRSX_SXOP((OP)` and no longer tests any
  raw `ARM64_OP_SXT*` opcode by hand. The generator has its own
  `python3 generate_arm64_ldrsx_op_spec.py --check` line in
  `kprog/formal/Makefile`.
- The load arm in `kprog/arm64/arm64_sim_local_bpf.h` (include added after the
  operand-source header) now routes through the generated selector: the derived
  `__a64_l_sxop` feeds the shared `ARM64_SIM_L_EXTREV_SIGNEXT` contract; the
  former inline ternary is gone. The macro name avoids collision with the
  pre-existing `KPROG_ARM64_LDRSX_HANDLED` / `KPROG_ARM64_LDRSX_LOAD_WIDTH`
  (Step 0061).
- Hand Lean `KProgFormal/Arm64LdrsxOp.lean` (imports
  `GeneratedArm64LdrsxOp`) states an independent code-keyed
  `arm64LdrsxOpSxOfCode` statement, the named sign-opcode list
  (`arm64LdrsxOpSignOps = [60, 47, 21]`) and load-code list
  (`arm64LdrsxOpLoadCodes = [54, 57, 63]`), and the membership spec predicate
  `arm64LdrsxOpSpec (op) := sxCode op ∈ arm64LdrsxOpSignOps`, and proves the
  generated `sxCode` equal to it (`arm64_ldrsx_op_refines`, `_sx_*` dispatch and
  range lemmas, `_code_determined`, `_selects_member`, `_load_codes_distinct`,
  `_sx_codes_distinct`, `_sx_not_load`, `_signbits_match_width` against the
  well-tested load-width contract, `_code_dispatch` with the exact numbers

- Host oracle `kprog/formal/test_arm64_ldrsx_op_host.c` declares the six

## Step 0129 — AArch64 ALU-arm operand-source-selection contract

- Scope: after Step 0128 the AArch64 dispatcher `ARM64_SIM_L_EXEC` routed every
  arm through a generated membership macro, both immediate/register
  operand-source selections through a generated selector, and the
  sign-extending load's derived opcode through a generated selector, but one
  raw opcode decision remained in the simulator: the generic ALU arm decided
  the right-hand operand *source* — decoded immediate versus second-source
  register read — with an inline `(OP) == ARM64_OP_ALU_IMM` test that fed the
  first argument of `KPROG_ARM64_ALU_RHS`. Shared JSON spec
  `kprog/formal/arm64_alu_operand_select_spec.json` (`schema_version` 1,
  operation `arm64AluOperandSelect`, `default` `register`, one selector `alu`
  with the `aluImm`=`ARM64_OP_ALU_IMM`=6 / `aluReg`=`ARM64_OP_ALU_REG`=7 pair)
  drives generator `kprog/formal/generate_arm64_alu_operand_select_spec.py`,
  which renders two code-drift rows and the source decision into
  `generated/arm64_alu_operand_select.h` and the `AluOperandSelectOp`
  inductive with its `code`/`immediate` tables into
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64AluOperandSelect.lean`.
- The generated macro `KPROG_ARM64_ALU_OPERAND_SELECT(OP)` is a statement
  expression (usable in the arm body but not at file scope or inside
  `_Static_assert`): it seeds its 0/1 result with `0` (the register form) and
  sets it to `1` on `case 6U` (the decoded-immediate form), with every other
  code falling through to the register form and never aborting. OP is
  evaluated exactly once. The immediate/register *value* choice itself stays
  the existing `KPROG_ARM64_ALU_RHS` contract (Step 0126), which takes this
  0/1 decision as its first argument; the new macro returns only the decision,
  so it composes with, rather than duplicates, that contract. The header also
  emits one `_Static_assert(ARM64_OP_X == N)` code-drift row per pair member.
  The generator's `--check` re-reads `kprog/arm64/arm64_sim.h` for both
  `ARM64_OP_*` numbers, asserts the spec table matches, asserts the selector
  order is `["alu"]` and the default is `register`, and asserts the live
  `ARM64_SIM_L_EXEC` region routes the source through
  `KPROG_ARM64_ALU_OPERAND_SELECT((OP)` and no longer tests any raw
  `(OP) == ARM64_OP_ALU_IMM` by hand. The generator has its own
  `python3 generate_arm64_alu_operand_select_spec.py --check` line in

- The ALU arm in `kprog/arm64/arm64_sim_local_bpf.h` (include added after the
  generic-operand header) now routes `KPROG_ARM64_ALU_RHS`'s first argument
  through the generated selector; the former inline opcode test is gone.
- Hand Lean `KProgFormal/Arm64AluOperandSelect.lean` (imports
  `GeneratedArm64AluOperandSelect` and the existing `GeneratedArm64AluOperand`
  / `Arm64AluOperandHandler`) states an independent named-list statement —
  `arm64AluOperandSelectImmOps = [.aluImm]`,
  `arm64AluOperandSelectRegOps = [.aluReg]`, and the membership predicate
  `arm64AluOperandSelectSpec op := op ∈ arm64AluOperandSelectImmOps` — and

## Step 0130 — x86-64 MULX width-keyed arm-selection contract

- Scope: after Step 0114 (XCHG) the x86-64 simulator's `X86_SIM_L_EXEC_MULX`
  macro still chose between its two bodies — the single 32x32-product split and
  the four-limb radix-`2^32` ladder — with an inline hand-written
  `if (__x86_l_width == X86_WIDTH_32)` test. Shared JSON spec
  `kprog/formal/x86_mulx_arm_spec.json` (`schema_version` 1, operation
  `x86MulxArmSelector`, selector `single_width_code_then_arm`, `width_code_bits`
  8, `opcode_define` `X86_OP_MULX` / `opcode` 57, `special_width_define`
  `KPROG_X86_MULX_SPECIAL_WIDTH` / `special_width_code` 4, and the two-arm table
  `singleProduct` (define `KPROG_X86_MULX_ARM_SINGLE_PRODUCT`, `is_special_width`
  1, effect `single_product_split`, class `w32`) / `limbLadder` (define
  `KPROG_X86_MULX_ARM_LIMB_LADDER`, `is_special_width` 0, effect
  `four_limb_ladder`, class `other`)) drives generator
  `kprog/formal/generate_x86_mulx_arm_spec.py`, which renders the arm defines,
  count, width-keyed selector, code-drift `_Static_assert`s and the
  `Arm`/`armOf`/`codeOfArm` table into `generated/x86_mulx_arm.h` and
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86MulxArm.lean`.
- The generated macro `KPROG_X86_MULX_ARM(WIDTH)` is a plain expression,
  `(((__u8)((WIDTH))) == KPROG_X86_MULX_SPECIAL_WIDTH ? ..._SINGLE_PRODUCT :
  ..._LIMB_LADDER)`, so it is usable both in the arm body and inside a
  `_Static_assert`; the input is evaluated once. The header also emits
  `_Static_assert` rows pinning `X86_OP_MULX`, the special-width code
  (`X86_WIDTH_32 == KPROG_X86_MULX_SPECIAL_WIDTH`), the arm count, the arm-code
  distinctness, and the width→arm mapping at 8/16/32/64. The generator's
  `--check` re-reads `kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h`, asserts the live
  `X86_SIM_L_EXEC_MULX` region routes through `KPROG_X86_MULX_ARM(__x86_l_width)`
  and no longer restates a raw `__x86_l_width == X86_WIDTH_32` test by hand, and
  rejects any spec drift. The generator has its own
  `python3 generate_x86_mulx_arm_spec.py --check` line in
  `kprog/formal/Makefile`.
- The `MULX` arm in `kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h` (include added after the
  `X86_OP_MULX` / `X86_WIDTH_*` decodes) now routes its body choice through the
  generated selector; the former inline width test is gone. The register reads,
  the low/high split, and the two destination writes stay in the composed arm
  body.
- Hand Lean `KProgFormal/X86MulxArmHandler.lean` imports
  `GeneratedX86MulxArm` and the existing `X86Width` / `X86MulxHandler` modules
  and states an independent literal selector `x86MulxArmSpec width := if width =
  x86WidthCodeSpec .w32 then .singleProduct else .limbLadder` plus the literal
  name list `x86MulxArmNamesSpec`. It proves the generated `armOf` equal to that
  independent statement (`x86_mulx_arm_refines`), the name table equal to the
  literal order (`x86_mulx_names_refine`), the exact arm count and code/name
  table lengths, the arm-code nodup, the single-iff-32 and ladder-iff-not-32
  characterisations (`x86_mulx_arm_single_iff_w32`,
  `x86_mulx_arm_ladder_iff_not_w32`), the width→arm behaviour over the four real
  width codes (`x86_mulx_arm_over_widths`), the `armOfCode` round-trip and

## Step 0131 — x86-64 BZHI/BZHI_MEM flag-block machine-checked contract

- Scope: after Step 0107 the x86-64 simulator's `X86_SIM_L_EXEC_BZHI_STEP`
  composition still wrote the `BZHI`/`BZHI_MEM` flag block by hand
  (`__x86_cf = __x86_l_count >= __x86_l_bits; __x86_zf = __x86_l_result == 0;
  __x86_sf = 0; __x86_of = 0;`). Shared JSON spec
  `kprog/formal/x86_bzhi_flags_spec.json` (`schema_version` 1, operation
  `x86BzhiFlags`, the two opcodes `bzhi` (`X86_OP_BZHI` / 52) and `bzhiMem`
  (`X86_OP_BZHI_MEM` / 53), `cf_source` `masked_count_at_least_width_bits`,
  `zf_source` `result_is_zero`, and the four-flag table `cf` = input
  `count_at_least_width_bits`, `zf` = input `result_is_zero`, `sf` = const
  `false`, `of` = const `false`) drives generator
  `kprog/formal/generate_x86_bzhi_flags_spec.py`, which renders the
  `KPROG_X86_SET_BZHI_FLAGS` do/while macro, the opcode-code `_Static_assert`s
  and the `Flags`/`eval` transition into `generated/x86_bzhi_flags.h` and
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86BzhiFlags.lean`.
- Unlike the `POPCNT` block (Step 0117), which takes one input (the
  width-narrowed source being zero, assigned to `ZF`), this block takes
  **two** inputs — the byte-masked count reaching the width's bit count
  (`CF`) and the cleared result being zero (`ZF`) — so a single-input
  logic-flag reuse would be wrong. The macro is a do/while, not a plain
  expression, because it writes four flag cells; the wrapper
  `X86_SIM_L_SET_BZHI_FLAGS(COUNT, BITS, RESULT)` feeds it
  `(COUNT) >= (BITS)` and `(RESULT) == 0`.
- The generator's `--check` re-reads `kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h`, asserts
  the live `X86_SIM_L_EXEC_BZHI_STEP` region still computes the masked-clear
  value (`kprog_x86_bzhi_value(`), routes its flag block through
  `X86_SIM_L_SET_BZHI_FLAGS(__x86_l_count, __x86_l_bits, ...)`, and no longer
  sets `__x86_cf` by hand, that the region is exactly one `#define`, and it
  rejects any spec drift. It has its own `python3
  generate_x86_bzhi_flags_spec.py --check` line in `kprog/formal/Makefile`.
- The routed wrapper lives in `kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h` (include added
  after the `X86_OP_BZHI_*` / `X86_WIDTH_*` decodes); the step's former
  hand-set flag block is gone. The register/memory reads, the masked-count bit
  clear, and the destination writeback stay in the composed step body.
- Hand Lean `KProgFormal/X86BzhiFlags.lean` imports `GeneratedX86BzhiFlags`
  and states the independent flag statement `x86BzhiSetFlagsSpec count result
  width` plus the independent `x86BzhiSetCfSpec` / `x86BzhiSetZfSpec`
  predicates. It proves the generated `eval` equal to that statement
  (`x86_bzhi_set_flags_refines`), the opcode/bit-width/source
  reconstruct-and-bound theorems, the flag-source equalities
  (`x86_bzhi_set_flags_cf_source_refines`,
  `x86_bzhi_set_flags_zf_source_refines`), the `SF`/`OF` clears
  (`x86_bzhi_set_flags_clears_sf_of`), the `CF`/`ZF` characterisations
  (`x86_bzhi_set_flags_cf_is_count_versus_width`,
  `x86_bzhi_set_flags_cf_independent_of_result`,
  `x86_bzhi_set_flags_zf_is_result_zero`,
  `x86_bzhi_set_flags_zf_real_sf_cleared`), and the threshold and
  below-width/count-behaviour witnesses at the 8- and 64-bit widths; the
  identifier prefix is `…BzhiSet…` so it does not collide with the
  `X86BzhiHandler` module's `x86BzhiFlagsSpec`. `KProgFormal.lean` imports the
  generated and hand modules.
- Host oracle `kprog/formal/test_x86_bzhi_flags_host.c` declares the
  `X86_OP_BZHI`/`X86_OP_BZHI_MEM` decodes from raw architectural values,
  includes `generated/x86_bzhi_flags.h`, drives the macro against a planted
  all-set flag state over every count≥bits × result-zero combination plus an
  all-set sentinel, and restates the block from the literal flag rules:
  `x86 bzhi flags host cross-check: OK (7 cases)`.
- Route oracle `kprog/formal/test_x86_bzhi_flags_route_host.c` includes the
  *simulator* header and drives the real `X86_SIM_L_EXEC(X86_OP_BZHI, ...)` and
  `X86_SIM_L_EXEC(X86_OP_BZHI_MEM, ...)` arms against an independent byte
  model, sweeping the count across every width's bit count
  (0/1/7/8/9/15/16/17/31/32/33/63/64/0xff) and the source across values whose
  bit-clear result is zero and nonzero, so both the `CF` (`count >= bits`) and
  `ZF` (`result == 0`) boundaries are numerically exercised; it compares the
  whole register file, its tags, and all four flags. The pre-existing
  `test_x86_bzhi_route_host.c` could not observe either boundary (its planted
  count is always ≥ the width's bit count and its result always nonzero, so
  `CF`≡1 and `ZF`≡0 there): `x86 bzhi flags route host cross-check: OK (36961
  cases)`.
- `make -C kprog/formal check` passes with the two new oracle rows raising the
  cross-check count from **169** (Step 0130 close) to **171**, zero `FAIL`.
  `make -C kprog/x86 micro-proofs-build` rebuilt all 31 workload-derived
  artifacts, all `ok`.
- Mutation harness `kprog/formal/build/mut_x86_bzhi_flags.py`, 81 mutations
  against the live tree, each caught after the four unmutated controls (`gen`,
  `lean_chain`, `host`, `route`) pass, restoring every watched file

## Step 0132 — x86-64 helper-call ladder routing through the generated slot selector

- Scope: after Step 0113 the generated `KPROG_X86_HELPER_SLOT` selector
  (spec `kprog/formal/x86_helper_dispatch_spec.json`, header
  `generated/x86_helper_dispatch.h`, hand Lean `KProgFormal/X86HelperDispatch.lean`)
  was static-asserted and proved, but it was referenced nowhere under
  `kprog/x86/`: the live `X86_SIM_BPF_CALL_ID` ladder still restated the
  binding as an inline `if (__x86_helper_id == X86_SIM_HELPER_bpf_*)
  X86_SIM_BPF_CALL_bpf_*();` chain, so a drift in the generated selector was
  not behaviourally observable. This step routes the ladder through the
  selector.
- `kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h`: `X86_SIM_BPF_CALL_ID(ID)` is now a
  `do { switch (KPROG_X86_HELPER_SLOT((__u64)(ID))) { case
  KPROG_X86_HELPER_SLOT(X86_SIM_HELPER_bpf_<name>): X86_SIM_BPF_CALL_bpf_<name>();
  break; ... default: X86_SIM_L_WRITE_REG_WIDTH(X86_RAX, 0, X86_WIDTH_64); break;
  } } while (0)` over the same seven arms in the same order
  (`bpf_map_lookup_elem .. bpf_ktime_get_ns`). Each arm keeps its own body
  macro; `X86_SIM_BPF_CALL_REG(REG)` is unchanged. The
  `#include "../formal/generated/x86_helper_dispatch.h"` is unchanged (one
  occurrence), so the header's per-id `_Static_assert`s still bind the 21
  hand-written `X86_SIM_HELPER_bpf_*` id values and the arm order to the
  generated table.
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_x86_helper_dispatch_spec.py`: the old
  `LADDER_ARM`/`LADDER_DEFAULT` shape checks are replaced by the routed-shape
  regexes `LADDER_SLOT` (`switch (KPROG_X86_HELPER_SLOT((__u64)(ID)))`),
  `LADDER_ARM` (`case KPROG_X86_HELPER_SLOT(<id define>): <body macro>();`) and
  `LADDER_DEFAULT`, plus a `LADDER_HAND_TEST` sentinel for the removed inline
  `__x86_helper_id == X86_SIM_HELPER_bpf_` comparison. `check_against_header()`
  now rejects a ladder that does not switch on the generated selector
  (`"x86 helper ladder does not switch on the generated slot selector"`) or that
  restates an inline helper-id comparison
  (`"x86 helper ladder restates an inline helper-id comparison"`). Its
  `python3 generate_x86_helper_dispatch_spec.py --check` Makefile line is
  unchanged.
- Hand Lean `KProgFormal/X86HelperDispatch.lean` appends an independent routed
  body spec `x86HelperDispatchRoutedBodySpec` (a `match` on the independent
  `x86HelperDispatchSlotOfSpec`) and five routing-composition theorems over it:
  `x86_helper_dispatch_route_labels_distinct` (the selector's slots over the
  armed ids are exactly `0 .. 6`, distinct and in order),
  `x86_helper_dispatch_route_body_is_table` (the routed table names the lookup
  body at slot 0 and the ktime body at slot 6),
  `x86_helper_dispatch_route_body_refines` (every armed id routes to the table
  body `getD i defaultBody`, and the zero id, the first id past the armed range
  `8`, the last named id `21`, and an id beyond the named space `22` all route
  to the default body), and two supporting slot/label lemmas. These compose the
  already-proved `x86_helper_dispatch_slotof_refines` with the routing shape.
  `KProgFormal.lean` already imports the generated and hand modules.
- Host oracle `kprog/formal/test_x86_helper_dispatch_host.c` (unchanged
  behaviour, stale "hand-written if/else-if ladder" doc comment fixed):
  `x86 helper dispatch host cross-check: OK (4100 cases)`. Route oracle
  `kprog/formal/test_x86_helper_dispatch_route_host.c` (doc comment fixed to
  name the routed selector): drives the real `X86_SIM_BPF_CALL_ID` `switch` and
  the routed `X86_SIM_BPF_CALL_REG` body over every armed id, the zero id, the
  unarmed named ids and beyond, and all 256 register numbers, comparing the
  whole changed register state against an independent id-to-body model:
  `x86 helper dispatch route host cross-check: OK (2882 cases)`.
- `make -C kprog/formal check` passes with **171** `cross-check: OK` rows and
  zero `FAIL` (the helper-dispatch oracle rows were already wired into the check
  target by Step 0113; only the ladder body changed, so the count is
  unchanged). `make -C kprog/x86 micro-proofs-build` rebuilt all 30
  workload-derived artifacts, all `ok`.
- Mutation harness `kprog/formal/build/mut_x86_helper_dispatch.py`, 83 mutations
  against the live tree, each caught after the four unmutated controls (`gen`,
  `lean_chain`, `host`, `route`) pass, restoring every watched file
  byte-for-byte between mutations and re-checking the baseline green at the
  end. Six semantics-preserving mutations (a resolved-but-equal generator root

## Step 0133 — x86-64 MOVX source-width resolution through the generated selector

- Scope: the generated `x86_movx_shape_spec.json` `source_width` block, its
  header `generated/x86_movx_shape.h`, and its hand Lean
  `KProgFormal/X86MovxShape.lean` existed and were static-asserted and proved,
  but the source-width resolution was restated by hand at both live `MOVZX`/
  `MOVSX` bodies in `kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h` as an inline
  `__x86_l_src_width = (AUX) ? (AUX) : __x86_l_width;` ternary, so a drift in
  the generated selector was not behaviourally observable. This step routes
  both bodies through the selector.
- `kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h`: both `MOVZX`/`MOVSX` bodies (the standalone
  shared macro `X86_SIM_L_EXEC_MOVX_REG`, and the `X86_OP_MOVZX_REG ||
  X86_OP_MOVSX_REG` arm) now compute
  `__u8 __x86_l_src_width = KPROG_X86_MOVX_SRC_WIDTH((AUX), __x86_l_width);`.
  `generated/x86_movx_shape.h` is already included (one occurrence), so the
  header's `_Static_assert`s bind the absent code, the four width-code
  identities, their distinctness, and the absent→effective fallback to the
  hand-written `X86_WIDTH_*` decodes.
- Spec `kprog/formal/x86_movx_shape_spec.json`: one `source_width` block
  `{"field":"aux","absent_code":0,"fallback":"effective_width"}`. Generator
  `kprog/formal/generate_x86_movx_shape_spec.py`: the routed-shape checks
  require the selector sentinel `KPROG_X86_MOVX_SRC_WIDTH((` in BOTH the macro
  and arm regions and reject the restated inline fallback
  `src_width = (AUX) ? (AUX)` in both; `load_width_codes()` re-derives the four
  `(name, code)` pairs from the public `kprog/formal/x86_width_spec.json` kernel
  and rejects any drift from the MOVX contract; `load()` rejects a non-canonical
  absent code, an absent code colliding with a width code, and an unknown
  fallback. The generator renders the Lean surface (`srcWidthField`,
  `srcWidthAbsentCode`, `srcWidthCodes`, `srcWidth(aux,effective)`) and the C
  surface (`KPROG_X86_MOVX_SRC_WIDTH_ABSENT_CODE`, a plain-ternary
  `KPROG_X86_MOVX_SRC_WIDTH(AUX, WIDTH)` so it is `_Static_assert`-usable, and

## Step 0134 — x86-64 condition-mnemonic decode through the generated contract

- Scope: the artifact encoder
  (`kprog/x86/micro-prog/generate_micro_sim_proofs.py`) restated its 36
  `jcc`/`cmovcc`/`setcc` condition mnemonics as a literal `CC_AUX` dict mapping
  each mnemonic to an `X86_CC_*` token, with no shared contract binding that
  table to the condition codes the simulator's `X86_CC_*` decodes name (whose
  numeric values are already the generated `x86_cond_spec.json` contract). A
  drift in either side was not observable. This step generates the table from
  one specification and cross-checks each row against the condition contract.
- Spec `kprog/formal/x86_cc_decode_spec.json`: schema_version 1, operation
  `x86CcDecode`, `families:["j","cmov","set"]`, the 12 encoder suffixes, and 36
  `{mnemonic,family,suffix,cond}` rows in `CC_AUX` order (`cond` equals
  `suffix`).
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_x86_cc_decode_spec.py`: module-level
  `FAMILIES`/`SUFFIXES`/`EXPECTED` re-checked element-wise; `cond_codes()` reads
  `x86_cond_spec.json` at load time (not imported) and `load()` rejects a suffix
  that names no condition, a mnemonic not equal to family+suffix, and a
  non-exhaustive/duplicated family. Emits the C header
  `generated/x86_cc_decode.h`, the Lean `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86CcDecode.lean`,
  and the encoder table `kprog/x86/micro-prog/generated_x86_cc_decode.py`
  (byte-identical to the deleted literal dict). `python3
  generate_x86_cc_decode_spec.py && ... --check` returns 0; the `--check` row is
  added at `kprog/formal/Makefile:66`.
- Generated C header: the 12 `_Static_assert(X86_CC_<S> == <n>U, ...)` code
  pins, `KPROG_X86_CC_DECODE_SUFFIX_{A..NS}` ordinals and `.._TEXT_*` strings, a
  plain-ternary `KPROG_X86_CC_DECODE_CC(SUFFIX)` selector (12 arms and a `0`
  default, so it is `_Static_assert`-usable), the per-suffix selection asserts,
  a suffix-count assert, a totality assert (an absent code reaches `0`), the
  family-prefix strings, and the 36 `.._MNEMONIC_*` strings.
- Hand Lean `KProgFormal/X86CcDecode.lean`: an independent 36-triple
  `ccMnemonicSpec`, the condition-contract `ccCondSpec`, and `ccSuffixSpec`,
  proving the generated projection equal to the independent enumeration
  (`x86_cc_decode_refines`), each code equal to the condition contract's code
  (`x86_cc_decode_code_matches_cond`), the reached suffixes exactly the
  non-parity names (`x86_cc_decode_suffixes_exact`), the mnemonic = family +
  suffix composition (`x86_cc_decode_mnemonic_composition`), the parity absence
  (`x86_cc_decode_parity_absent`), the codes exactly the non-parity codes
  (`x86_cc_decode_codes_exact`), and the three families each reaching all 12
  conditions (`x86_cc_decode_families_uniform`). `lake build
  KProgFormal.GeneratedX86CcDecode && lake env lean
  KProgFormal/X86CcDecode.lean` returns 0.
- Encoder routing `kprog/x86/micro-prog/generate_micro_sim_proofs.py`: the
  literal `CC_AUX` dict is replaced by `from generated_x86_cc_decode import
  CC_AUX`; all 15 consumer sites resolve to the import. `make -C kprog/x86
  micro-proofs-build` rebuilt all 30 workload-derived artifacts, all `ok`, and a
  full SHA-256 snapshot of the encoder output directory showed no drift.
- Host oracle `kprog/formal/test_x86_cc_decode_host.c`: restates the 36
  mnemonics with their family/suffix decomposition, the 12 suffixes, and the
  suffix→code map by hand, then drives the generated selector over every suffix
  code, an out-of-range slice, each mnemonic's hand-derived suffix, and the
  parity absence: `x86 cc decode host cross-check: OK (152 cases)`.
- `make -C kprog/formal check` passes with **172** `cross-check: OK` rows and
  zero `FAIL` (the new generator `--check`, the two Lean rows, and the host
  oracle rows were added; 171→172).
- Mutation harness `kprog/formal/build/mut_x86_cc_decode.py`, 30 mutations
  against the live tree, each caught after the four unmutated controls (`gen`,
  `lean_chain`, `host`, `encoder`) pass, restoring every watched file
  byte-for-byte between mutations and re-checking the baseline green at the end.
  It includes the load-time condition-contract cross-check (a code shift in
  `x86_cond_spec.json` makes the generator stale) and the encoder detector that
  imports the live `CC_AUX`. Two semantics-preserving mutations (a
  resolved-but-equal generator root path, an added hand-module namespace
  comment) SURVIVE as required.
- Paper `docs/kprog-simulator-in-ebpf/sections/4-safety.tex` adds the x86-64
  condition-mnemonic decode paragraph and extends the covered-slices list with
  the condition-mnemonic decode contract (paper commit pushed to `main`).

## Step 0135 — AArch64 condition-mnemonic decode through the generated contract

- Scope: the artifact encoder
  (`kprog/arm64/micro-prog/generate_micro_sim_proofs.py`) restated its 17
  condition mnemonics as a literal `COND` dict mapping each mnemonic to an

  condition codes the simulator's `ARM64_COND_*` decodes name (whose numeric
  values are already the generated `arm64_cond_spec.json` contract). Unlike
  x86, two mnemonics alias one code (`hs`→`ARM64_COND_CS`, `lo`→`ARM64_COND_CC`),
  so the alias fact is itself proved. A drift in either side was not
  observable. This step generates the table from one specification and
  cross-checks each row against the condition contract.

  `arm64CcDecode`, and 17 `{mnemonic,cond,alias}` rows in `COND` order; `alias`
  is true only for `hs`/`lo`.
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_arm64_cc_decode_spec.py`: module-level
  `EXPECTED` re-checked element-wise; `cond_codes()` reads `arm64_cond_spec.json`
  at load time (not imported); `load()` rejects a mnemonic that names no
  condition, a canonical (non-alias) mnemonic set that is not exactly the
  contract's condition order, an alias naming no canonical condition, and a
  duplicate mnemonic. Emits the C header `generated/arm64_cc_decode.h`, the Lean
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64CcDecode.lean`, and the encoder table
  `kprog/arm64/micro-prog/generated_arm64_cc_decode.py` (byte-identical to the
  deleted literal dict). `python3 generate_arm64_cc_decode_spec.py && ... --check`
  returns 0; the `--check` row is added at `kprog/formal/Makefile:63`.
- Generated C header: the 15 `_Static_assert(ARM64_COND_<C> == <n>U, ...)` code
  pins, `KPROG_ARM64_CC_DECODE_MNEMONIC_{EQ..AL}` ordinals and `.._TEXT_*`
  strings, mnemonic/condition count defines, a plain-ternary
  `KPROG_ARM64_CC_DECODE_COND(MNEMONIC)` selector (17 arms and a `0` default, so
  it is `_Static_assert`-usable), the per-mnemonic selection asserts, count
  asserts, a totality assert (an absent code reaches `0`), and the alias asserts
  (`hs`→`CS`, `lo`→`CC`).
- Hand Lean `KProgFormal/Arm64CcDecode.lean`: an independent 17-triple
  `ccArm64MnemonicSpec`, the condition-contract `ccArm64CondSpec`, and
  `ccArm64AliasSpec`, proving the generated projection equal to the independent
  enumeration (`arm64_cc_decode_refines`), each code equal to the condition
  contract's code (`arm64_cc_decode_code_matches_cond`), the reached conditions
  exactly the contract's fifteen (`arm64_cc_decode_conds_exact`), the canonical
  mnemonics covering each condition once (`arm64_cc_decode_canonical_covers`),
  the aliases exactly `hs`/`lo` (`arm64_cc_decode_aliases_exact`), the alias
  codes equal to their canonical spellings (`arm64_cc_decode_alias_same_code`),
  and that an alias is only ever `hs`/`lo`
  (`arm64_cc_decode_alias_not_canonical`). `lake build
  KProgFormal.GeneratedArm64CcDecode && lake env lean
  KProgFormal/Arm64CcDecode.lean` returns 0.
- Encoder routing `kprog/arm64/micro-prog/generate_micro_sim_proofs.py`: the
  literal `COND` dict is replaced by `from generated_arm64_cc_decode import
  COND`; all consumer sites resolve to the import.
- Host oracle `kprog/formal/test_arm64_cc_decode_host.c`: restates the 17
  mnemonics and the mnemonic→code map by hand, then drives the generated
  selector over every mnemonic code, a dense out-of-range slice, the
  alias-equal-code facts, and a per-condition reachability sweep:
  `arm64 cc decode host cross-check: OK (76 cases)`.
- `make -C kprog/formal check` passes with **173** `cross-check: OK` rows and
  zero `FAIL` (the new generator `--check`, the two Lean rows, and the host

- Mutation harness `kprog/formal/build/mut_arm64_cc_decode.py`, 32 mutations

## Step 0136 — AArch64 per-program compact helper-table contract through the generated spec

- Scope: the artifact encoder
  (`kprog/arm64/micro-prog/generate_micro_sim_proofs.py`) restated its 61 BPF
  helper-ident rows as a literal `HELPER_IDENTS` dict mapping each kernel id to
  a helper name, with no shared contract binding that table to the simulator's
  `ARM64_SIM_BPF_CALL_*` bodies (whose forwarding macros additionally pin the
  compact slot of the target they forward to) or to the per-program compact
  helper table the encoder emits (which renumbers a program's called helpers to
  their 1-based lexicographic rank over the used names). Unlike x86, the
  compact slot a forwarding target pins is the *target's* rank over the full
  61-name table, so the five `KPROG_ARM64_HELPER_DELEGATE_*` pins are proved
  facts, not a restatement. A drift in any artifact was not observable. This
  step generates the table from one specification and cross-checks every row
  and delegate slot against an independent enumeration.
- Spec `kprog/formal/arm64_helper_idents_spec.json`: schema_version 1, operation
  `arm64HelperIdents`, and 61 `{id,name}` rows in id-sorted order.
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_arm64_helper_idents_spec.py`: `load()`
  re-reads the simulator header on every `--check` and rejects a row whose name
  is not a sim-header body macro (the body-macro set must biject the 61 spec
  names), a duplicate kernel id or name, and a forwarding target that names no
  source or target macro. Emits the C header `generated/arm64_helper_idents.h`
  (the `KPROG_ARM64_HELPER_ROW` by-id selector with its out-of-range default and
  the five `KPROG_ARM64_HELPER_DELEGATE_*` compact-slot pins), the Lean
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64HelperIdents.lean`, and the encoder table
  `kprog/arm64/micro-prog/generated_arm64_helper_idents.py`. `--check`
  returns 0; the `--check` row is added at `kprog/formal/Makefile:64`.
- Generated C header `kprog/formal/generated/arm64_helper_idents.h`:
  `KPROG_ARM64_HELPER_IDENTS_COUNT 61U`, `KPROG_ARM64_HELPER_DELEGATE_COUNT
  5U`, the `KPROG_ARM64_HELPER_ROW(KERNEL_ID)` 1-based by-id ordinal (0
  out-of-range, per-row and out-of-range `_Static_assert`s), and the five
  delegate compact-slot pins (`_BPF_GET_CURRENT_TASK_BTF 11U`,
  `_BPF_TASK_PT_REGS 11U`, `_BPF_COPY_FROM_USER_TASK 2U`,
  `_BPF_IMA_FILE_HASH 25U`, `_BPF_MAP_LOOKUP_PERCPU_ELEM 32U`).
- Hand Lean `kprog/formal/KProgFormal/Arm64HelperIdents.lean`: an independent
  61-pair `helperIdentsSpec` and a `allHelperIdents` constructor enumeration, with
  theorems `helper_idents_refines` (the generated `(id,name)` projection equal to
  the independent enumeration), `helper_idents_names_nodup`,
  `helper_idents_ids_strictly_increasing`, `helper_delegate_ranks` (each
  forwarding target's pinned slot equals its 1-based lexicographic rank over the
  full 61-name table), and `helper_slot_ranks` (every name's own slot equals its
  rank); all `native_decide`. `lake build
  KProgFormal.GeneratedArm64HelperIdents && lake env lean
  KProgFormal/Arm64HelperIdents.lean` returns 0.
- Encoder routing `kprog/arm64/micro-prog/generate_micro_sim_proofs.py`: the
  61-entry inline `HELPER_IDENTS` dict is replaced by `from
  generated_arm64_helper_idents import HELPER_IDENTS`; all consumer sites resolve
  to the import.
- Host oracle `kprog/formal/test_arm64_helper_idents_host.c`: restates the 61
  rows, the out-of-range default, the two counts, and the five forwarding slots
  by hand, then drives the generated row selector over every kernel id, the
  out-of-range default, the two counts, and the five forwarding slots against
  an independent restatement:
  `arm64 helper idents host cross-check: OK (69 cases)`.
- `make -C kprog/formal check` passes with **174** `cross-check: OK` rows and
  zero `FAIL` (the new generator `--check`, the two Lean rows, and the host
  oracle rows were added; 173→174).
- Mutation harness `kprog/formal/build/mut_arm64_helper_idents.py`, 29
  mutations against the live tree, each caught after the four unmutated
  controls (`gen`, `lean_chain`, `host`, `encoder`) pass, restoring every
  watched file byte-for-byte between mutations and re-checking the baseline
  green at the end: 27 of the 29 change the oracle, the generator check, or a
  refinement theorem---five specification distortions, two simulator-body macro
  add/remove and a retargeted forwarding macro, two generator-table changes,
  five generated-C header distortions, two generated-Lean changes, four
  hand-refinement changes, three encoder-table changes, an encoder-import
  rename, and two regenerated generator/render drifts---while two
  genuine-equivalence rewrites (a resolved-but-equal generator root path and an
  added hand-module namespace comment) SURVIVE as required.
- Paper `docs/kprog-simulator-in-ebpf/sections/4-safety.tex` adds the AArch64
  helper-ident and compact-slot composition paragraph and extends the
  covered-slices list with the helper-ident and compact-slot selection contract

## Step 0137 — AArch64 stack-write slot-tag action selection through the generated contract

- Scope: the AArch64 simulator's `ARM64_SIM_L_STACK_WRITE_TAG` write helper
  (`kprog/arm64/arm64_sim_local_bpf.h`) selected between three slot-tag
  actions from a closed pair of facts — whether the access width is 64 bits
  and whether the stack slot is 8-aligned — with no contract binding that
  selection to a generated selector or to Lean. The hand `KPROG_ARM64_STACK_TAG(`
  gate and the three-arm selection lived only in the write-helper body, so
  a drift in the action selection was not observable. This step generates
  the 3-way action selector from one specification and routes the live
  write helper through the generated `KPROG_ARM64_STACK_WRITE_TAG_ACTION`
  selector, removing the hand gate from the write path (Step 0137 delta
  from 0124, which kept a hand gate plus a parallel contract); the
  read-side slot-tag helper still uses the hand gate and is unchanged.
- Spec `kprog/formal/arm64_stack_write_tag_action_spec.json`: schema_version 1,
  operation `arm64StackWriteTagAction`, and three actions — `writeWordAndTag`
  (code 0, effect `word_write_tag`), `clearTagAndWriteBytes` (code 1,
  effect `clear_tag_bytes`), `writeBytesNoTag` (code 2, effect
  `bytes_no_tag`) — plus four cases classifying every (isW64, isAligned)
  fact pair into its action.
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_arm64_stack_write_tag_action_spec.py`:
  `load()` re-reads the sim header on every `--check` and rejects a spec
  that does not biject the expected actions/cases table, an effect that
  names no storage effect, and a write region that names no generated
  selector or still names a hand `KPROG_ARM64_STACK_TAG(` gate. Emits the
  C header `generated/arm64_stack_write_tag_action.h` (the
  `KPROG_ARM64_STACK_WRITE_TAG_ACTION(IS_W64, IS_ALIGNED)` 3-way selector,
  the action-code defines, and the count, distinctness, and selection
  `_Static_assert`s) and the Lean
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64StackWriteTagAction.lean`. `--check`
  returns 0; the `--check` row is added at `kprog/formal/Makefile:67`.
- Generated C header `kprog/formal/generated/arm64_stack_write_tag_action.h`:
  `KPROG_ARM64_STACK_WRITE_TAG_ACTION_COUNT 3U`, the three action-code
  defines (`…_WRITE_WORD_AND_TAG 0U`, `…_CLEAR_TAG_AND_WRITE_BYTES 1U`,

- Hand Lean `kprog/formal/KProgFormal/Arm64StackWriteTagActionShape.lean`:

## Step 0138 — AArch64 stack slot-tag read source selection through the generated contract

- Scope: the AArch64 simulator's `ARM64_SIM_L_STACK_READ_TAG` read helper
  (`kprog/arm64/arm64_sim_local_bpf.h`) returned the tag of a stack slot
  read from a closed pair of facts — whether the read width is 64 bits and
  whether the stack slot is 8-aligned — and picked the tag source by hand:
  the slot's word in the per-slot tag array when 64-bit and aligned, the
  scalar marker otherwise, with the read-side `KPROG_ARM64_STACK_TAG(`
  slot-tag predicate as the inline gate. This step generates the 2-way
  source selector from one specification and routes the live read helper
  through the generated `KPROG_ARM64_STACK_READ_TAG_SOURCE` selector,
  removing the hand gate from the read path. This is the read-side mirror
  of Step 0137's write-side 3-way action and closes the read/write
  symmetry of the stack-tag family: the `.stackTagArray` source fires on
  the same fact pair the 0121 `KPROG_ARM64_STACK_TAG` gate and the 0137
  write helper's word-and-tag action fire on.
- Spec `kprog/formal/arm64_stack_read_tag_source_spec.json`: schema_version 1,
  operation `arm64StackReadTagSource`, and two sources — `stackTagArray`
  (code 0, effect `slot_tag_array`), `scalarDefault` (code 1, effect
  `scalar_default`) — plus four cases classifying every (isW64, isAligned)
  fact pair into its source.
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_arm64_stack_read_tag_source_spec.py`:
  `load()` re-reads the sim header on every `--check` and rejects a spec
  that does not biject the expected sources/cases table, an effect that
  names no storage effect, and a read region that names no generated
  selector or still names a hand `KPROG_ARM64_STACK_TAG(` gate. Emits the

## Step 0141 — AArch64 vector lane extra-offset selection through the generated contract

- Scope: the AArch64 simulator's shared vector memory step
  `ARM64_SIM_L_DQ_MEM_STEP` (`kprog/arm64/arm64_sim_local_bpf.h`), which moves
  the SIMD register's halves to or from memory one lane at a time and computed
  each moved lane's *extra* byte offset by hand through a nested ternary on
  `__a64_vreg_p == 0U` (is this the first plan position) and
  `__a64_dq_lanes > 1U` (does the transfer have a high lane at all), yielding
  `0 / 8 / 0`: the first-lane offset zero for the first plan position, one
  64-bit lane stride for the second position of a `.Q0` transfer, and the
  base offset zero when the plan has only one position. This step generates
  the 3-way offset selector from one specification and routes the step
  through the generated `KPROG_ARM64_DQ_MEM_EXTRA` selector, removing the
  hand nested ternary from the step. It is the per-lane *offset* companion to
  the 0141 DQ lane plan (which owns the access direction, lane count, and lane
  stride) and the 0054 vector half plan (which owns which state field each
  lane lands in): the `.highLane` offset fires exactly on the closed fact pair
  the two preceding contracts already consume.
- Spec `kprog/formal/arm64_dq_mem_extra_spec.json`: schema_version 1,
  operation `arm64DqMemExtraOffset`, selector
  `first_lane_then_zero_else_high_lane_present_then_high_lane_stride_else_zero`,
  and three outcomes --- `firstLane` (code 0, offset 0, effect
  `plan_first_lane_offset`), `highLane` (code 1, offset 8, effect
  `plan_high_lane_offset`), `singleLane` (code 2, offset 0, effect
  `plan_single_lane_offset`) --- plus four cases classifying every
  (is first lane, high present) fact pair into its outcome.
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_arm64_dq_mem_extra_spec.py`: `load()`
  re-reads the sim header on every `--check` and rejects a spec that does not
  biject the expected outcomes/cases table (including the exact `[0, 1, 2]`
  code order and the three-outcome count), a case whose outcome does not match
  the independent 3-way selection, and a vector memory step region that names
  no generated selector or still names the hand first-position ternary. Emits
  the C header `generated/arm64_dq_mem_extra.h` (the
  `KPROG_ARM64_DQ_MEM_EXTRA(IS_FIRST_LANE, HAS_HIGH_LANE)` plain-ternary
  3-way selector, the outcome-code and byte-offset defines, and the count,
  distinctness, exact-code, high-lane-stride, base-offset, and four fact-pair
  selection `_Static_assert`s) and the Lean
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64DqMemExtra.lean`. `--check` returns 0; the
  `--check` row is added at `kprog/formal/Makefile:71`.
- Generated C header `kprog/formal/generated/arm64_dq_mem_extra.h`:
  `KPROG_ARM64_DQ_MEM_EXTRA_COUNT 3U`, the three outcome-code defines
  (`…_FIRST_LANE_BYTES 0U`, `…_HIGH_LANE_BYTES 1U`, `…_SINGLE_LANE_BYTES 2U`),
  the three byte-offset defines with the `_BYTES_OFFSET` suffix
  (`…_FIRST_LANE_BYTES_OFFSET 0U`, `…_HIGH_LANE_BYTES_OFFSET 8U`,

## Step 0142 — AArch64 memory index-value source selection through the generated contract

- Scope: the AArch64 simulator's memory address offset
  `ARM64_SIM_L_MEM_BASE_OFF` (`kprog/arm64/arm64_sim_local_bpf.h`), which
  computes the byte offset a load/store adds to its base register. Its index
  *presence* is already generated (Step 0102,
  `generated/arm64_mem_index.h`), but the *value* the present index register
  contributes was still picked by hand through a ternary on the computed
  `__a64_mbo_has_index` fact --- the source-modified index register value when
  the addressing mode carries an index register, a literal zero when it does
  not (the sentinel index operand `ARM64_REG_NONE`, whose byte tag is
  `KPROG_ARM64_MEM_INDEX_SENTINEL`). This step generates the 2-way

## Step 0143 — AArch64 vector memory step's half state-field selection through the generated contract

- Scope: the AArch64 simulator's shared vector memory step
  `ARM64_SIM_L_DQ_MEM_STEP` (`kprog/arm64/arm64_sim_local_bpf.h`), which moves

  fields (`__a64_v0` / `__a64_v0_hi`). The moved lane's *offset* was already
  generated (Step 0141, `KPROG_ARM64_DQ_MEM_EXTRA`, which owns the per-lane
  extra offset and, via `KPROG_ARM64_VREG_HALF_OFFSET`, computes

  hand on both the load and the store arm through

## Step 0144 — AArch64 write-register width body-selection through the generated contract

- Scope: the AArch64 simulator's writeback body
  `ARM64_SIM_L_WRITE_REG_WIDTH` (`kprog/arm64/arm64_sim_local_bpf.h`), which
  every GPR write in the simulator routes through. It first masks the value to
  the access width (`KPROG_ARM64_APPLY_WIDTH`, owned by the Step-0075
  `arm64_width.h` contract) and then picked the writeback body by hand from a
  single closed fact --- whether the access width code is the 32-bit code ---
  through `if ((WIDTH) == ARM64_WIDTH_32)` selecting the narrow truncating body
  (`ARM64_SIM_L_WRITE_REG32_CASE`, storing `(__u32)__a64_l_next`) vs the
  full-value body (`ARM64_SIM_L_WRITE_REG64_CASE`, storing `__a64_l_next`).
  This step generates the 2-way selector from `arm64_write_arm_spec.json` into
  the C `generated/arm64_write_arm.h` (the `KPROG_ARM64_WRITE_ARM` plain-ternary
  selector, the `…_FULL` / `…_NARROW` arm codes, the count, distinctness,
  exact-code, and per-width selection `_Static_assert`s) and
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64WriteArm.lean`, and routes the body through the
  generated selector ---
  `if (KPROG_ARM64_WRITE_ARM((WIDTH) == ARM64_WIDTH_32) ==
  KPROG_ARM64_WRITE_ARM_NARROW)` --- so the hand width test is out of the body.
  The `ARM64_SP` branch and the `KPROG_ARM64_REG_WRITABLE` guard stay outside
  the selector (destination identity, not the width body choice).
- Semantic note: because the value is masked to the width *before* the body
  choice, the two bodies are observationally equal for every width the
  simulator reaches (at the 32-bit code the masked value's upper 32 bits are
  already zero; at the 8/16/64-bit codes the full body writes the already-masked
  value). The split is a genuine no-op on state, so only a wrong *selector code*
  or a *swapped body assignment* is observable; the route oracle's expectation
  is width-body-sensitive for exactly this reason.
- Spec `kprog/formal/arm64_write_arm_spec.json`: schema_version 1, operation
  `arm64WriteArm`, selector `w32_then_narrow_else_full`, w32_define
  `ARM64_WIDTH_32`, w32_code 4, and two arms --- `full` (arm_define
  `KPROG_ARM64_WRITE_ARM_FULL`, body `full_width_writeback`) and `narrow`
  (arm_define `KPROG_ARM64_WRITE_ARM_NARROW`, body `narrow_width_writeback`) ---
  plus two cases classifying the (is w32) fact into its arm.
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_arm64_write_arm_spec.py`: `load()` re-reads
  the sim header on every `--check` and rejects a spec that does not biject the
  expected arms/cases table (including the exact `[0, 1]` code order and the
  two-arm count), a case whose arm does not match the independent 2-way
  selection, and a writeback-body region that names no generated selector or
  still names the hand `if ((WIDTH) == ARM64_WIDTH_32)` gate. Emits the C header
  `generated/arm64_write_arm.h` (the `KPROG_ARM64_WRITE_ARM(IS_W32)`
  plain-ternary 2-way selector, the arm-code defines, and the count,
  distinctness, exact-code, and per-width selection `_Static_assert`s) and the
  Lean `KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64WriteArm.lean`. `--check` returns 0; the
  `--check` row is added at `kprog/formal/Makefile:74`.
- Generated C header `kprog/formal/generated/arm64_write_arm.h`:
  `KPROG_ARM64_WRITE_ARM_W32 4U`, `KPROG_ARM64_WRITE_ARM_COUNT 2U`, the two
  arm-code defines (`KPROG_ARM64_WRITE_ARM_FULL 0U` /
  `KPROG_ARM64_WRITE_ARM_NARROW 1U`), the plain-ternary 2-way selector macro,
  and the count, distinctness, exact-code, and per-width selection
  `_Static_assert`s (cross-pinning `ARM64_WIDTH_32` to the generated `_W32`

- Generated Lean `kprog/formal/KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64WriteArm.lean`: the
  `Arm` type, `armCount := 2`, `w32Code := 4`, the arm-name and code tables,

- Hand Lean `kprog/formal/KProgFormal/Arm64WriteArmShape.lean`: independent

## Step 0145 — x86-64 write-register width body-selection through the generated contract

- Scope: the x86-64 simulator's writeback body
  `X86_SIM_L_WRITE_REG_WIDTH_SHIFT` (`kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h`), which
  every GPR write in the simulator routes through. It first resolves the
  decoded operand width through the Step-0075 `x86_width_effective` bridge
  (`KPROG_X86_WIDTH_EFFECTIVE`, owned by `generated/x86_width.h`) and then
  picked the writeback body by hand from a ladder over the *resolved* width
  code --- `if (__x86_wr_width == X86_WIDTH_8)` writing one byte lane
  (`X86_SIM_L_WRITE_REG8_VALUE_CASE`), the 16-bit code the low word
  (`X86_SIM_L_WRITE_REG16_VALUE_CASE`), the 32-bit code the low dword
  (`X86_SIM_L_WRITE_REG32_VALUE_CASE`), and every other code the full qword
  (`X86_SIM_L_WRITE_REG64_VALUE_CASE`). This step generates the 4-way
  width-code selector from `x86_write_width_arm_spec.json` into the C
  `generated/x86_write_width_arm.h` (the `KPROG_X86_WRITE_WIDTH_ARM` nested
  ternary selector, the four `KPROG_X86_WRITE_WIDTH_ARM_B8`/`_B16`/`_B32`/`_B64`
  arm codes, the count, distinctness, per-width selection, and absent-code
  `_Static_assert`s) and `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86WriteWidthArm.lean`, and
  routes the body through the generated selector ---
  `if (KPROG_X86_WRITE_WIDTH_ARM(__x86_wr_width) ==
  KPROG_X86_WRITE_WIDTH_ARM_B8)` withdrawing to the hand ladder --- so the hand
  width ladder is out of the body.
- Semantic note: unlike Step 0144 (whose value was pre-masked before the body
  choice, making its two bodies observationally equal), the width here is
  applied *inside* each body's write macro (`KPROG_X86_WRITE_REG8` writes a
  single byte lane, `KPROG_X86_WRITE_REG16` the low word, `KPROG_X86_WRITE_REG32`
  the low dword, `KPROG_X86_WRITE_REG64` the whole register) and `__x86_wr_next`
  is not pre-masked, so the four bodies write the destination register
  genuinely differently. A wrong selector code or a swapped body therefore
  changes the written register bytes and is observable in the route oracle.
- Spec `kprog/formal/x86_write_width_arm_spec.json`: schema_version 1, operation
  `x86WriteWidthArmSelector`, selector `resolved_width_code_then_write_body`,
  width_code_bits 8, and four arms --- `b8` (arm_define
  `KPROG_X86_WRITE_WIDTH_ARM_B8`, width_code 1, body `byte_lane_writeback`,
  case_macro `X86_SIM_L_WRITE_REG8_VALUE_CASE`, width_class narrow), `b16`
  (`…_B16`, code 2, `word_writeback`, `X86_SIM_L_WRITE_REG16_VALUE_CASE`,
  narrow), `b32` (`…_B32`, code 4, `dword_writeback`,
  `X86_SIM_L_WRITE_REG32_VALUE_CASE`, narrow), and `b64` (`…_B64`, code 8,
  `qword_writeback`, `X86_SIM_L_WRITE_REG64_VALUE_CASE`, full).
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_x86_write_width_arm_spec.py`: `load()`
  re-reads the sim header on every `--check` and rejects a spec that does not
  biject the expected arms table (including the exact width-code order and the
  four-arm count), a width-class ladder that is not
  `["narrow", "narrow", "narrow", "full"]`, a default arm that is not the qword
  one, and a write-width region that names no generated selector, omits any of
  the four bodies or their case macros, or still contains the hand width ladder
  `if (__x86_wr_width == X86_WIDTH_8)`. Emits the C header
  `generated/x86_write_width_arm.h` (the `KPROG_X86_WRITE_WIDTH_ARM(CODE)`
  nested-ternary 4-way selector, the four arm-code defines, and the count,
  distinctness, per-width selection, and absent-code `_Static_assert`s) and the
  Lean `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86WriteWidthArm.lean`. `--check` returns 0; the
  `--check` row is added at `kprog/formal/Makefile:133`.
- Generated C header `kprog/formal/generated/x86_write_width_arm.h`:
  `KPROG_X86_WRITE_WIDTH_ARM_COUNT 4U`, the four arm-code defines
  (`KPROG_X86_WRITE_WIDTH_ARM_B8 0U` / `_B16 1U` / `_B32 2U` / `_B64 3U`), the
  nested-ternary 4-way selector macro, and the count, distinctness, per-width
  selection (each `X86_WIDTH_*` code to its own body), and absent-code (code 0
  to the default qword body) `_Static_assert`s.
- Generated Lean `kprog/formal/KProgFormal/GeneratedX86WriteWidthArm.lean`: the
  `Arm` type, `armCount := 4`, `widthCodeBits := 8`, the arm-name and code

## Step 0146 — x86-64 stack byte-ladder per-lane activation contract

- Scope: the x86-64 simulator's stack write helper `X86_SIM_L_STACK_WRITE` and
  stack read helper `X86_SIM_L_STACK_READ` (`kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h`)
  narrowed a resolved access to the byte arena `__x86_stack_mem.b[]` through a
  little-endian byte ladder whose eight lane writes (the write helper) and eight
  lane assemblies (the read helper) were gated by hand-written
  `__x86_stw_width` / `__x86_str_width` `>= X86_WIDTH_16` / `>=
  X86_WIDTH_32` / `== X86_WIDTH_64` tests restated at each lane. The width set
  is closed (the four `X86_WIDTH_*` codes) and the activation is monotone: an
  access of `n` bytes touches exactly lanes `0..n-1`, so the width's active-lane
  mask has its low `n` bits set. Unlike the AArch64 Step 0124 write-only helper,
  the x86-64 read helper is itself an eight-lane assemble ladder, so this step
  is one contract routed through **two** helper bodies with identical width
  gates.
- Shared spec `kprog/formal/x86_stack_write_lanes_spec.json` (schema_version 1,
  operation `x86StackWriteLanes`, selector `width_mask_low_lanes_active`)
  enumerates the four widths — `w8`/`w16`/`w32`/`w64` with codes `1/2/4/8`,
  byte counts `1/2/4/8` and masks `1/3/15/255` — the eight lanes
  (`lane0..lane7`, indices `0..7`), and the per-width activation row
  (`n` leading `true`s, the rest `false`).
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_x86_stack_write_lanes_spec.py` re-derives the
  live stack helper text from the simulator header and requires it to route its
  lanes through the generated predicate `KPROG_X86_STACK_WRITE_LANE_ACTIVE(`
  while keeping the byte-lane extraction/write (`KPROG_X86_STACK_BYTE(`), the
  byte arena (`__x86_stack_mem.b[`), the width-narrowing value
  (`KPROG_X86_STACK_APPLY_WIDTH(`) and the little-endian assembly
  (`KPROG_X86_STACK_ASSEMBLE(`), and dropping all six hand gates
  (`HAND_GATE_16`/`_32`/`_STR_16`/`_STR_32`/`_64`/`_STR_64`). It emits the
  plain-expression, `_Static_assert`-safe C header
  `generated/x86_stack_write_lanes.h` (the `?:`-chain mask macro
  `KPROG_X86_STACK_WRITE_MASK`, the eight lane-number defines,
  `.._LANE_SLOTS 8U`, `.._LANE_COUNT`, `.._LANE_ACTIVE(WIDTH, LANE) =
  ((__u8)((MASK(WIDTH) >> (LANE)) & 1U))`, four width-code asserts, eight
  mask/count asserts and thirty-two full activation asserts) and the Lean table
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86StackWriteLanes.lean` (inductive `Width`/`Lane`,
  `widthCode`, `byteCount`, `widthMask`, `laneIndex`,
  `laneActive (width lane) := decide ((widthMask width >>> laneIndex lane) &&& 1
  = 1)`, `activeLanes`, `laneSpec`, `laneActive_refines`,
  `activeLanes_length`, `widthMask_is_low_bits`). `--check` returns 0; the
  `--check` row is added at `kprog/formal/Makefile:134`.
- Hand refinement `KProgFormal/X86StackWriteLanesShape.lean` states an
  independent literal construction (`x86StackWriteLanesCountSpec`/`MaskSpec`/
  `LaneSpec`) and proves the shape/theorem set, including
  `x86_stack_write_lanes_refines` (the generated mask-bit activation equals the
  independent `laneIndex < byteCount` bound), `_spec_iff`, `_mask_refines`,
  `_count_refines`, `_lane_refines`, `_length`, `_mask_is_low_bits`,
  `_monotone` (an active lane stays active at every wider access — exactly the
  nested `>= 16`/`>= 32`/`== 64` gate structure), `_lane0_always`,
  `_above_never`, `_codes_match_width` (against `x86WidthCodeSpec`),
  `_matches_store_bytes` (against the generated `GeneratedX86MemAccess.byteCount`
  and `GeneratedX86Width.code` — the two modules that carry the byte counts and
  codes, since x86 has no single module carrying both), `_lane_is_byte_lane`
  (against the `GeneratedX86StackArena` byte), `_over_widths`, and the three
  canonical examples; the hypothesis-carrying monotonicity and above-never
  theorems are closed by `revert h <;> cases <;> decide`. `lake build
  KProgFormal.GeneratedX86StackWriteLanes` and `lake env lean
  KProgFormal/X86StackWriteLanesShape.lean` return 0.
- Routed bodies: the write ladder's eight lane `if`s now test
  `KPROG_X86_STACK_WRITE_LANE_ACTIVE(__x86_stw_width, k)` and the read ladder's
  eight lane-assembly `if`s test
  `KPROG_X86_STACK_WRITE_LANE_ACTIVE(__x86_str_width, k)`; the byte-window
  arithmetic, the scalar first-lane write/read and the little-endian
  composition are unchanged, and the ladder bodies are not re-indented. The
  generated header is included at `x86_sim_local_bpf.h:39`, after the other
  generated arm includes. The public signatures and every caller site are
  unchanged.
- Two host oracles, both wired into `kprog/formal/Makefile` immediately after
  the write-width-arm pair:
  - `test_x86_stack_write_lanes_host.c` includes the generated header
    (compiling it against hand-written `X86_WIDTH_*` values), checks every
    `(width, lane)` pair's mask bit, count and activation against an
    independent literal oracle, and checks the mask is each width's low-bit set
    --- `x86 stack write lanes host cross-check: OK (291 cases)`.
  - `test_x86_stack_write_lanes_route_host.c` includes the simulator header
    (`X86_SIM_ENABLE_STACK`) and drives the real `X86_SIM_L_STACK_WRITE` at
    every width and many arena offsets, then the real `X86_SIM_L_STACK_READ`
    (the essential round-trip detector for the read-side ladder), comparing the
    whole stack byte image against independent models of the activation (an
    `n`-byte access touches exactly bytes `0..n-1`, higher bytes untouched) and
    of the little-endian assembly --- `x86 stack write lanes route host
    cross-check: OK (1401654 cases)`.
- Gate `make -C kprog/formal check` rc=0. Baseline was **192** for Step 0145;
  Step 0146 adds the stack-write-lanes generator `--check`, the Lean pair, and
  the host and route oracles (192→194). `make -C
  kprog/arm64 micro-proofs-build` rebuilt all 30 workload-derived artifacts,
  all `ok`.
- Mutation harness `kprog/formal/build/mut_x86_stack_write_lanes.py`, 63
  mutations against the live tree, each caught after the four unmutated controls
  (`gen`, `lean_chain`, `host`, `route`) pass, restoring every watched file
  byte-for-byte between mutations and re-checking the baseline green at the end:
  eight spec defects (operation/schema/selector/width-code/width-bytes/mask/

  (operation/selector/width-code/width-bytes/lane-index/Lean-path/C-header-path/

- Paper `docs/kprog-simulator-in-ebpf/sections/4-safety.tex` adds the x86-64

## Step 0147 — x86-64 ALU-token flag-body-selection contract

- Scope: the x86-64 simulator's flag-setting entry
  `X86_SIM_L_SET_ALU_FLAGS` (`kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h`), the helper every
  arithmetic/logical handler routes its flag production through, which picked
  the flag body by hand from a chain over the `X86_ALU_*` operation token. The
  token set is the sixteen `X86_ALU_*` codes (an 8-bit field), and the mapping
  from token to flag body is *not* injective: the ADD and ADC codes both reach
  the add body, the SHL/SHR/SAR/ROL codes all reach the shift body, and the
  INC/DEC families reach the add/sub bodies but then restore the incoming carry
  (the architectural `INC`/`DEC` carry preservation). This step generates the
  token→body selection from `x86_alu_flag_arm_spec.json` into the C
  `generated/x86_alu_flag_arm.h` (the `KPROG_X86_ALU_FLAG_ARM(ALU)`
  nested-ternary selector, the ten `KPROG_X86_ALU_FLAG_ARM_*` arm codes, the
  count, the sixteen token-code drift checks, distinctness, per-token selection,
  default and unknown-token `_Static_assert`s) and
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86AluFlagArm.lean`, and routes the body through the
  generated selector --- `switch (KPROG_X86_ALU_FLAG_ARM((ALU)))` over the ten
  `case KPROG_X86_ALU_FLAG_ARM_*` bodies with the logic body as the `default:` ---
  so the hand token ladder is out of the body. This is the x86-side mirror of
  the AArch64 Step 0066 (the token-keyed selector style is Step 0116's).
- Semantic note: the selector takes the *raw* `X86_ALU_*` token; the SBB/ADC
  handler split stays in each caller's outer guard, so the body is total over
  every code through the `default:` logic arm and there is no unsupported case.
  The increment/decrement arms keep the `__x86_l_old_cf` save/restore; the not
  arm keeps `KPROG_X86_PRESERVE_FLAGS()`; the multiply arm keeps the CF/OF-only
  body; a wrong selector code, a swapped body, a dropped carry-restore or a
  dropped token is numerically observable in the route oracle.
- Spec `kprog/formal/x86_alu_flag_arm_spec.json`: schema_version 1, operation
  `x86AluFlagArmSelector`, selector `alu_token_then_flag_body`, alu_code_bits 8,
  and ten arms --- `add` (`…_ARM_ADD`, codes `[0, 15]` = ADD/ADC, body
  `add_flags`, case `X86_SIM_L_SET_ADD_FLAGS`, no restore, effect
  `sum_flags`), `inc` (`…_ARM_INC`, `[10]` = INC, `add_flags`,
  `X86_SIM_L_SET_ADD_FLAGS`, restore, `increment_flags_preserve_cf`), `dec`
  (`…_ARM_DEC`, `[13]` = DEC, `sub_flags`, `X86_SIM_L_SET_SUB_FLAGS`, restore,
  `decrement_flags_preserve_cf`), `sub` (`…_ARM_SUB`, `[1]`, `sub_flags`,
  `X86_SIM_L_SET_SUB_FLAGS`, `difference_flags`), `sbb` (`…_ARM_SBB`, `[12]`,
  `sbb_flags`, `X86_SIM_L_SET_SBB_FLAGS`, `borrow_difference_flags`), `neg`
  (`…_ARM_NEG`, `[14]`, `sub_flags`, `X86_SIM_L_SET_SUB_FLAGS`,
  `negation_flags`), `not` (`…_ARM_NOT`, `[11]`, `preserve_flags`,
  `KPROG_X86_PRESERVE_FLAGS`, `flags_unchanged`), `shift` (`…_ARM_SHIFT`,
  `[5, 6, 7, 8]` = SHL/SHR/SAR/ROL, `shift_flags`,
  `X86_SIM_L_SET_SHIFT_FLAGS`, `shift_flags`), `imul` (`…_ARM_IMUL`, `[9]`,
  `imul_flags`, `X86_SIM_L_SET_IMUL_FLAGS`, `multiply_overflow_flags`), and
  `logic` (`…_ARM_LOGIC`, `[2, 3, 4]` = XOR/OR/AND, `logic_flags`,
  `X86_SIM_L_SET_LOGIC_FLAGS`, `bitwise_flags_default`).
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_x86_alu_flag_arm_spec.py`: `load()`
  cross-checks each `alu_defines[i]` against `x86_alu_decode_spec.json`'s
  `operations` (the mnemonic lower-cased → `X86_ALU_` + upper), asserts the two
  collapses (ADD/ADC→add, SHL/SHR/SAR/ROL→shift) and the total coverage of all
  sixteen codes; `check_against_header()` re-reads the sim header on every
  `--check` and requires the flag-setting region to route through
  `KPROG_X86_ALU_FLAG_ARM((`, name every non-default arm's case, keep the
  `__x86_l_old_cf` save/restore, the `1`/`0` operands and
  `KPROG_X86_PRESERVE_FLAGS()`, have `SET_LOGIC_FLAGS` as the default body, and
  drop the hand token ladder (`X86_ALU_ADD ||`, …). Emits the C header
  `generated/x86_alu_flag_arm.h` and the Lean
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86AluFlagArm.lean`. `--check` returns 0; the `--check`
  row is added at `kprog/formal/Makefile:138`.
- Generated C header `kprog/formal/generated/x86_alu_flag_arm.h`:
  `KPROG_X86_ALU_FLAG_ARM_COUNT 10U`, the ten arm-code defines
  (`…_ARM_ADD 0U` / `_INC 1U` / `_DEC 2U` / `_SUB 3U` / `_SBB 4U` / `_NEG 5U` /
  `_NOT 6U` / `_SHIFT 7U` / `_IMUL 8U` / `_LOGIC 9U`), the nested-ternary
  selector macro, and the count, sixteen token-code drift, distinctness,
  per-token selection, default and unknown-token (`0xffU` → logic)
  `_Static_assert`s.
- Generated Lean `kprog/formal/KProgFormal/GeneratedX86AluFlagArm.lean`: the
  `Arm` type, `armCount := 10`, `aluCodeBits := 8`, the arm-name and code
  tables, `codeOfArm`/`aluCodesOfArm`/`flagBodyOfArm`/`caseMacroOfArm`/
  `cfRestoreOfArm`/`effectOfArm`, the token-keyed `armOf`, and `armOfCode`.
- Hand Lean `kprog/formal/KProgFormal/X86AluFlagArmShape.lean`: independent
  literal statements of the token ladder (built on the ALU contract's own
  `x86AluCodeSpec` codes), the ten arm names, flag bodies, case macros and
  effects, with theorems `x86_alu_flag_arm_refines` (the generated `armOf`
  equals the independent token ladder), `_names_refine`, `_codes_length`/
  `_names_length`, `_codes_nodup`, `_over_tokens`, `_collapses` (ADD/ADC→add and
  SHL/SHR/SAR/ROL→shift), `_of_code_roundtrip`, `_of_code_beyond_is_none`,
  `_code_bits_is_8`, `_count_is_10`, `_flag_bodies`, `_case_macros`,
  `_cf_restores` (exactly the increment/decrement families),
  `_effects`/`_effects_distinct`, `_ladder_total`, `_case_dispatch` and
  `_default_is_logic`; all `native_decide`/`rfl`/`decide`. `lake build
  KProgFormal.GeneratedX86AluFlagArm` and `lake env lean
  KProgFormal/X86AluFlagArmShape.lean` return 0.
- Sim-header routing `kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h`: the flag-setting body now
  selects its body through the generated `KPROG_X86_ALU_FLAG_ARM((ALU))`
  selector, the hand token ladder is out of the body, and the include
  `#include "../formal/generated/x86_alu_flag_arm.h"` is added beside the other
  generated arm includes (`x86_sim_local_bpf.h:40`), while the
  `__x86_l_old_cf` save/restore, the INC/DEC carry restores, and the `(LHS, RHS,
  RESULT, ALU, WIDTH)` signature are unchanged, so the six call sites

- Host oracle `kprog/formal/test_x86_alu_flag_arm_host.c`: restates the token-keyed

- Route oracle `kprog/formal/test_x86_alu_flag_arm_route_host.c`: declares the

## Step 0148 — x86-64 dispatch-family token-membership contract

- Scope: the x86-64 simulator's dispatch-family membership gates
  `KPROG_X86_MOV_LOAD_PTR_HANDLED`, `KPROG_X86_MOVX_REG_HANDLED`,
  `KPROG_X86_MOV_LOAD_HANDLED`, `KPROG_X86_MOV_STORE_HANDLED`,
  `KPROG_X86_ALU_IMM_HANDLED`, `KPROG_X86_ALU_REG_HANDLED`,
  `KPROG_X86_CMP_IMM_HANDLED`, `KPROG_X86_CMP_REG_HANDLED`,
  `KPROG_X86_CMP_MEM_HANDLED`, and
  `KPROG_X86_DOUBLE_SHIFT_HANDLED` (`kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h`),
  which the dispatcher's `else if` chain tests in that order, each a
  hand-written disjunction over `X86_OP_*` tokens (a member of one family
  is dispatched by exactly one gate: the families are disjoint and their
  order is fixed by the chain). This step generates the ten
  token-membership tests from `x86_dispatch_family_spec.json` into the C
  `generated/x86_dispatch_family.h` (the ten `KPROG_X86_<F>_HANDLED(OP)`
  membership macros, the twenty-four `X86_OP_* == code` token-code drift
  asserts binding the hand-written decode to the generated sets, and the
  twenty-four per-token coverage asserts naming every member through its
  own gate) and `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86DispatchFamily.lean`, and routes
  each family arm through its generated gate so the hand disjunctions are
  out of the body. This is the x86-side mirror of the AArch64
  dispatch-family style (the token-keyed selector style is Step 0116's;
  the arm-code selector style is Step 0147's, but here membership is the
  contract, not body selection, so the generated artefact is a family of
  membership macros, one per gate, in the gate order the dispatcher reads).
- Semantic note: the ten families are disjoint over the simulated opcode
  set; `KPROG_X86_<F>_HANDLED(OP)` is true for exactly the family's member
  tokens, so the ordered dispatcher chain has at most one taken gate per
  opcode and an opcode outside every family falls through every gate to the
  chain's tail (a member token misrouted to another arm, a gate-order swap
  that exposes a different body to the same tuple, a family overlap, or a
  dropped token is distinguishable in the route oracle, where each routed
  family arm is executed under a pinned whole-state against an independent
  model).
- Spec `kprog/formal/x86_dispatch_family_spec.json`: schema_version 1,
  operation `x86DispatchFamily`, and the ten families with their gate macro

## Step 0149 — x86-64 dispatch-singleton opcode-membership contract

- Scope: the dispatcher's remaining forty-three single-member gates in
  `kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h` --- the `X86_SIM_L_EXEC` arms that test a
  single opcode with a raw hand comparison instead of a shared family
  macro: the CALL ladder's four encodings and the register protocol call,
  the register immediate/move arms, the MOVBE load/store pair, the XMM0
  load/store pair, LEA, the five memory-source ALU arms, the compare
  register-vs-memory arm, both CMOV arms, both SETCC arms, BSWAP, POPCNT,
  both SHIFTX arms, both RORX arms, both BZHI arms, the three BT arms, the
  two IMUL-immediate arms, MULX, REP MOVS, the ANDN pair, XCHG, DIV, PUSH
  and POP. This step generates those forty-three single-opcode membership
  tests from `x86_dispatch_singleton_spec.json` into the C
  `generated/x86_dispatch_singleton.h` (the forty-three
  `KPROG_X86_DISP_<NAME>_HANDLED(OP)` plain-expression membership macros,
  the forty-three `X86_OP_* == code` token-code drift asserts binding the
  hand-written decode to the generated sets, and the forty-three per-token
  coverage asserts naming every singleton through its own gate) and
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86DispatchSingleton.lean`, and routes each
  singleton arm through its generated gate so the hand comparisons are out
  of the body. This is the x86-side mirror of the AArch64
  dispatch-singleton style (the arm64 singleton family is Step 0126),
  completing the dispatcher so every gate in the `X86_SIM_L_EXEC` chain is
  either a generated ten-family membership macro (Step 0148) or one of
  these generated singleton macros.
- Spec `kprog/formal/x86_dispatch_singleton_spec.json`: schema_version 1,
  operation `x86DispatchSingleton`, and the forty-three singletons with
  their name, code, op macro, and gate macro in the dispatcher's own arm
  order, with `X86_OP_*` numbers 0..59 as pinned by the spec generator
  against `kprog/x86/x86_sim.h`.
- Generator `kprog/formal/generate_x86_dispatch_singleton_spec.py`:
  `load()` requires the JSON to equal the generator's expected table
  verbatim (`EXPECTED`), asserts per-opcode code drift against
  `kprog/x86/x86_sim.h`'s `#define X86_OP_* 0b0..U` definitions and
  rejects duplicate names; `check_against_header()` re-reads the sim
  header on every `--check`, requires the dispatcher chain to route the
  forty-three singleton arms through the generated gates (`NOP` keeps its

  requires the live dispatcher to not keep any other raw

  the `--check` row is added at `kprog/formal/Makefile:140`.
- Hand Lean `kprog/formal/KProgFormal/X86DispatchSingleton.lean`:
  independent named member lists for each of the forty-three singletons

  disjunctions), with theorems `x86_disp_singleton_<name>_refines` per
  singleton (the generated `<name>Handled` equals the independent list
  membership), `x86_dispatch_singleton_member_handled` (a singleton member
  is handled by some gate), `x86_dispatch_singleton_nonmember_unhandled`
  (an opcode outside every singleton is handled by no gate),
  `x86_singleton_code_dispatch` (the `code` table equals the forty-three

  `x86_singleton_code_in_range`, `x86_singleton_codes_nodup`, the

## Step 0151 — x86-64 shift-flag route oracle and mutation harness

- Code `589f0296b` (superproject `master`): adds
  `kprog/formal/test_x86_shift_flags_route_host.c` and three `check` rows.
  The route oracle includes `kprog/x86/x86_sim_local_bpf.h` and drives the
  `X86_SIM_L_SET_SHIFT_FLAGS` wrapper as dispatched from
  `case KPROG_X86_ALU_FLAG_ARM_SHIFT` in `X86_SIM_L_SET_ALU_FLAGS`,
  reproducing the wrapper's own input derivation (width narrowing via
  `X86_SIM_L_EFFECTIVE_WIDTH`, `x86_width_bits`/`x86_width_mask`, the sign
  bit, and the masked `x86_shift_count`), and compares the full register
  file plus CF/ZF/SF/OF against an independent walk written from the
  generated Lean semantics.  Coverage: 4 shift tokens × 5 width codes ×
  8 lhs values × 11 rhs values × 7 result values = 6,504,961 routed cases;
  result line `x86 shift flags route host cross-check: OK (6504961 cases)`.
  The value tables pin rhs=0 (all four flags preserved), rhs=1 (the
  OF-at-count-one boundary), rhs=31/32/33 and rhs=63/64 (mask-count
  boundaries), and 0xffffffff, with 0x80/0x8000000000000000 lhs values
  covering the CF last-shifted-bit and SAR sign-saturation paths.
- The third new `check` row types
  `KProgFormal/GeneratedX86ShiftFlags.lean` directly, matching the 0147
  Generated-Lean + hand-Lean row pairs.  Observed gate arithmetic: a `make
  -C kprog/formal check` run emits one `OK (` row per oracle run only (the

  rows do not carry an OK marker.  Baseline had 200 OK rows; after adding

  `x86 shift flags route host cross-check: OK (6504961 cases)` is the only
  addition (diff of `grep "OK ("` against the 0150 baseline log).

  (evidence only; `build/` is gitignored and no mutator is tracked):

  drives the *real* inlined IMUL arm bodies of `X86_SIM_L_EXEC`
  (`X86_OP_IMUL_IMM` (0x38) and `X86_OP_IMUL_MEM_IMM` (0x41)) over 5 width
  codes × 8 left operands × 6 immediate artifacts × 2 incoming flag seeds
  for the flagged form plus 5 width codes × 5 AUX memory-width codes (the
  absent code plus the four real codes) × 8 heap fill patterns × 6
  immediate artifacts × 3 addressing modes (no index, index at scale 1,
  index at scale 8) × 2 flag seeds for the memory form = 7,680 routed
  cases, each checked for full register/tag/flag state plus the unchanged
  heap image (261,121 rows); the register form's right operand is the
  whole immediate sign-extended at the FLAGS-resolved width (the upper
  half participates), the memory form re-resolves the store immediate
  through the `KPROG_X86_IMMEDIATE_VALUE` 32-bit shape and multiplies by
  the loaded value signed-extended at the memory width, and the flag
  funnel pin restates the generated `KPROG_X86_SET_IMUL_FLAGS` division
  with the magnitudes taken from the RAW left operand narrowed to the
  FLAGS width while the product uses the memory-width-extended left
  operand (the split a w=32/memory-width-1 case with a `2^30`-shaped
  right operand distinguishes numerically).
- **Semantic finding recorded, oracle restates it.** While
  cross-checking the memory form the oracle surfaced that
  `X86_SIM_L_EXEC_IMUL_MEM_IMM` passes its pre-extracted store-half
  displacement through the whole-immediate slot of
  `X86_SIM_L_READ_MEM_VALUE(..., STORE_DISP=1)`, whose `STORE_DISP`
  branch applies `x86_store_imm_disp` a second time, so the effective
  displacement is `(s32)((u64)(s32)(imm >> 32) >> 32)` rather than the
  single wrap `(s32)(imm >> 32)` (visible whenever the bits above bit 31
  of the store displacement are nonzero); six byte-level probes confirmed
  the divergence for the four store-half artifacts with high bits set.
  Per the route-oracle convention (the model restates what the generated
  body computes), the oracle was fixed to the two-step wrap — the sim
  header is untouched — and the pin is documented in both the oracle
  comment and the model's inline comment.

  `X86_SIM_L_READ_REG(SRC)` → `(DST)`),
  `simlocal_imul_imm_rhs_width_drift` (whole-immediate rhs
  sign-extension width `__x86_l_width` → `X86_WIDTH_8`; an earlier plan
  narrowing the extension to 8 bits via the plain constant was proven a
  genuine equivalence — the funnel narrows the right magnitude at the
  body width before the product and the writeback masks at the same

  and the mutant instead skips the extension down, making immediates
  with bits at or above bit 7 distinct),
  `simlocal_imul_mem_lhs_raw_drift` (memory-form product left operand
  drops the memory-width sign extension), and
  `simlocal_imul_mem_flags_raw_mw_drift` (flag-funnel left magnitude

## Step 0176 — AArch64 MOVK move-wide insertion mutation coverage

- Scope: the AArch64 move-wide insertion value
  `KPROG_ARM64_MOVK_INSERT` --- the low 16 bits of the immediate inserted at
  one of the four architectural columns 0/16/32/48 while every other
  destination bit is kept, dispatched from the simulator's
  `KPROG_ARM64_DISP_MOVK_HANDLED` arm through `ARM64_SIM_L_MOVK_VALUE`
  (`arm64_sim_local_bpf.h:490` threads the column from
  `ARM64_SIM_L_SHIFT(AUX)`); the column is the packed AUX word's lane-2
  shift field, exactly the architectural column for `ARM64_AUX_MOVK(S)`
  (`KPROG_ARM64_AUX(0U, 0U, (S), 0U)`), which the generator re-checks by
  regex on every `--check`. The hand Lean refinement pins the independent
  `arm64MovkValueSpec` (the destination with the 16-bit column cleared or'd
  with the narrowed immediate shifted into place --- deliberately not a
  restatement of the generated mask pair), the refinement of the generated
  `value` over every column/value pair (`bv_decide`), the width-narrowed
  composition over every width, the closed column set (0 v 16 v 32 v 48),
  the four-column dispatch, and six `native_decide` examples.

  mutation rows) over five contract files --- the column spec
  (`arm64_movk_spec.json`: four columns, `arm64Movk`, schema 1), its
  generator (`generate_arm64_movk_spec.py`: expected-column table, name
  and order pins, coverage/handled/mask-ladder case recipes, the
  `ARM64_AUX_MOVK` lane-2 alias regex re-checked against

  generated C switch macro (`generated/arm64_movk.h`: the
  `KPROG_ARM64_MOVK_HANDLED` guard, four coverage static assertions, the
  per-column case arms, the mask seed, the insert statement, and the

  (`KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64Movk.lean`; the four-member `MovkShift`

  (`KProgFormal/Arm64Movk.lean`). Three detectors, no regen stage and no
  sim-header stage --- the wrapper threads the column through one
  `ARM64_SIM_L_MOVK_VALUE` call, so the host oracle reaches the macro

  (`generate_arm64_movk_spec.py --check`), `lean_chain` (`lake build
  KProgFormal.GeneratedArm64Movk` then `lake env lean
  KProgFormal/Arm64Movk.lean`), and `host` (the 20,145-case

- Result: `TOTAL 74 mutations, 0 failures`, `ALL AS EXPECTED`, exit 0.
  68 mutants catch (gen 30, lean_chain 19, host 18 --- three of the host

- Scope: the AArch64 packed-AUX layout contract --- the 32-bit operand word

  (`KPROG_ARM64_AUX` plus the four `KPROG_ARM64_AUX_B0..B3` decoders and the
  `KPROG_ARM64_AUX_REG_NONE` sentinel, `arm64_aux_spec.json` /

  `KProgFormal/GeneratedArm64Aux.lean` / `KProgFormal/Arm64Aux.lean`), with
  the six simulator packer aliases (`ARM64_AUX`, `_ALU`, `_SHIFT`, `_MOVK`,
  `_MEM`, `_BITFIELD`, `_CCMP` in `arm64_sim.h`) and seven simulator decoder
  aliases (`ARM64_SIM_L_MOD`..`_CCMP_NZCV` in `arm64_sim_local_bpf.h`) thin
  aliases of that one layout, so a repaint of any alias sheet must surface
  through the real macros the oracles compile. The hand Lean refinement pins
  the four decoders against the independent `(aux >>> 8k) &&& 0xff`

  generated C header, the generated Lean module, the hand Lean refinement,

  KProgFormal/Arm64Aux.lean`), `host` and `route` (both oracles recompiled

  contract, which decides which register write carries the provenance tag
  at doubleword width; this harness covers the tag-dropping value path
  every other member and width resolves through.
- Harness: `build/mut_arm64_csel.py` (untracked, 112 single-anchor mutation
  rows) over nine contract files --- the value spec, its generator, the
  generated C header, the generated Lean module, the hand Lean refinement,

  sheet. Four detectors: `gen` (`generate_arm64_csel_spec.py --check`

  KProgFormal/Arm64Csel.lean`), `host` (mux oracle recompiled per row,
  with a forked child for the unsupported-opcode abort which is defined
  behavior, not fatal), and `route` (width-effective scanner recompiled
  per row, in-process only --- the absent-width semantics are defined, not
  fatal). No regen stage: the spec pins its constants, so a stale-`--check`
  pair is not cleanly applicable.
- Result: `TOTAL 112 mutations, 0 failures`, `ALL AS EXPECTED`, exit 0.
  105 mutants catch (gen 43 --- 17 spec rejections, 21 generator drifts,
  5 generated-header drifts surfaced by re-render; lean_chain 31 --- 11
  generated-Lean and 20 hand-Lean; host 26; route 5 --- 3 sim-local

## Step 0220 — x86 IMUL flags mutation coverage

## Step 0221 — x86 little-endian memory access mutation coverage

  width's bytes (byte i contributes bits 8i..8i+8) then narrows with the
  width mask; store masks the value then writes the width's bytes,
  leaving bytes at or above the width untouched. Spec JSON pins the
  whole metadata template byte-for-byte (little endianness, zero_is_64
  width rule, load/store/byte_rule wordings, four width rows); generator
  renders the Lean byteCount/assemble/load/storeByte/store module and

  restates assemble/load/storeByte through the width bridge and proves
  the three refinements, the byte-count law, and two native_decide
  examples (0x12345678 w32 load, 0xaabb w16 store bytes); X86MemByte
  and the refine theorems are consumed by the ten-plus memory handlers.
